trap-negation-contrast.evidence: Pure-data table; ten trap categories n/a. FULLY RECOMPUTED at 40 dps. Recursion sigma^k = A_k sigma + B_k with A_{k+1} = h A_k + B_k, B_{k+1} = A_k, h = q - 1/q, tr_M = A_k z + B_k. With the EXCISED convention C (z = sqrt(q)/(q+1) = 0.4993203) the five entries come out 0.49932, 1.10439, 0.730204, 1.25704, 0.993002 - matching all five printed values 0.499 / 1.104 / 0.730 / 1.257 / 0.993 exactly. Under the canonical convention D (z = q^3/(q^2+1) = 0.6126880) they would be 0.612688, 1.12809, 0.848527, 1.30548, 1.12145 - ALL FIVE would differ in the first printed digit. The table is therefore definitively convention-C and needs re-derivation under D. Column 3 also verified: 1/(q;q)_k = -9.09268, 39.18372, -106.6073, 205.8243, -300.5192 against the printed -9.09, +39.18, -106.61, +205.82, -300.52, all correct; and the ratio column reproduces column2/column3 in every row. Pin: proton and muon q_0 agree to the 7th significant figure here, so the table CANNOT distinguish the two pins at the printed precision; 1.1097 would show at k=3 onward and is excluded.
